question.text: A PM sees the 2-year G-Sec at 6.5% and the 10-year at 7.3%. The 'Term Spread' is:

explanation.text: The Logic: Term Spread = Long-term yield − Short-term yield = 7.3% − 6.5% = 0.8% = 80 bps. The Trap: 130 bps is an arithmetic mistake; 0 is obviously wrong; 7.3% is the long rate alone. Cross-Exam Context: XV, IV, XIII all test term spread; XXI-B uses it for yield-curve calls. Manager's Pro-Tip: Widening term spreads often precede economic recovery; inverting spreads historically precede recessions — watch the 10-2 spread.
